# Thermostat replacement procedure

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove air cleaner components, disconnect water hose, then unbolt thermostat housing for replacement. [t1682]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the air cleaner and duct assembly.
2. Disconnect the water hose from the thermostat inlet housing.
3. Unbolt and remove the thermostat housing to access the unit.

_Procedure reported by [t1682]._

## Tools

- [Partial] Wrenches [t1682]

## Tips & gotchas

- Consider removing the radiator out of the way for easier access if tensioner brackets are in the path. [t1682]
- Use a liquid gasket (specifically Permatex 51813 or 51817) on the hose-to-housing connection. [t1682]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using a solid paper gasket instead of RTV for the housing-to-hose fitting, which can lead to leaks. [t1682]
- Stripping threads in the engine mating surface due to limited accessibility and tight angles when tightening bolts. [t1682]
